questions.q: **MIND : EOJN :: WORK : ?**
questions.solution: Write MIND backwards: D N I M. Move each letter +1: E O J N — that is the given code. Do the same with WORK: backwards K R O W, then +1 gives **LSPX**. (XPSL is WORK + 1 without reversing — the trap.)
questions.shortcut: Code starts with the letter after the word's LAST letter (D to E): reverse first, then shift.
Second number just above n²: 57 − 49 = 8 = 7 + 1, 91 − 81 = 10 = 9 + 1.

questions.q: **Cardiology : Heart :: Nephrology : ?**
questions.solution: Cardiology is the branch of medicine dealing with the heart; **nephrology** deals with the **kidney** (Greek *nephros*). Liver is hepatology, nerves is neurology and lungs is pulmonology.
questions.shortcut: Branch of medicine : organ it treats.

questions.q: Find the odd number pair: **3 – 28, 5 – 126, 4 – 65, 6 – 215**
questions.solution: In 3 – 28, 5 – 126 and 4 – 65 the second number is (first)³ **+ 1**: 27 + 1, 125 + 1, 64 + 1. For 6 the rule gives 216 + 1 = 217, but the pair shows 215 (= 6³ − 1). So **6 – 215** is odd.
questions.shortcut: Recognise cubes 27, 64, 125, 216 and check the sign of the ±1.

questions.q: Find the odd one out: **Ganga, Godavari, Narmada, Krishna**
questions.solution: Ganga, Godavari and Krishna flow eastward and drain into the **Bay of Bengal**. The **Narmada** flows westward through a rift valley and drains into the **Arabian Sea**, so it is the odd one.
questions.shortcut: Sort rivers by where they meet the sea: east-flowing vs west-flowing.

questions.q: Find the next term: **1, 2, 6, 15, 31, 56, ?**
questions.solution: Differences: 2 − 1 = 1, 6 − 2 = 4, 15 − 6 = 9, 31 − 15 = 16, 56 − 31 = 25 — these are 1², 2², 3², 4², 5². The next difference is 6² = 36, so the next term is 56 + 36 = **92**.
questions.shortcut: When first differences look irregular, test them against squares/cubes.

questions.q: Find the next term: **AZ, CX, FU, JQ, ?**
questions.solution: First letters A, C, F, J move +2, +3, +4, so next is +5: J + 5 = **O**. Second letters Z, X, U, Q move −2, −3, −4, so next is −5: Q − 5 = **L**. Answer **OL** (check: O and L are opposite letters, like every pair here).
questions.shortcut: Each pair is an opposite pair (sum 27): find the first letter, the second is its opposite.

questions.q: Find the next term: **K2, M6, P18, T54, ?**
questions.solution: Letters: K to M is +2, M to P is +3, P to T is +4, so next is +5: T (20) + 5 = 25 = **Y**. Numbers: 2, 6, 18, 54 — each is ×3, so next is 54 × 3 = **162**. Next term: **Y162**.
questions.shortcut: Treat letters and numbers as two separate series.

questions.q: In a certain code language, **'sky is blue'** is written as **'ka mo ti'**, **'blue ink pen'** is written as **'ti re su'**, and **'pen is red'** is written as **'su mo na'**. What is the code for **'sky'**?
questions.solution: Compare sentences two at a time. 'blue' is common to the 1st and 2nd sentences, and so is 'ti' — blue = ti. 'is' is common to the 1st and 3rd, and so is 'mo' — is = mo. (Similarly pen = su from the 2nd and 3rd.) In 'sky is blue' = 'ka mo ti', the codes mo and ti are taken, so sky = **ka**.
questions.shortcut: Common word ↔ common code; the leftover code is the answer.

questions.q: In a certain code language, **LAMP** is written as **MCPT**. How will **FISH** be written in that language?
questions.solution: Compare letter by letter: L to M is +1, A to C is +2, M to P is +3, P to T is +4 — the shift equals the letter's position. For FISH: F + 1 = G, I + 2 = K, S + 3 = V, H + 4 = L — **GKVL**.
questions.shortcut: Write the gap under each letter; +1, +2, +3, +4 is a favourite CGL pattern.

questions.q:
Which two signs should be **interchanged** to make the following equation correct?

**20 ÷ 4 + 3 × 6 − 2 = 25**
questions.shortcut: Try the options one by one with BODMAS; drop any swap that makes a fraction appear.

questions.solution: Row rule: (first)² − (second)². Check: 49 − 9 = 40 and 36 − 16 = 20. So 8² − 5² = 64 − 25 = **39**. (89 comes from adding the squares; 40 from (a + b) × 4, which fails row 2.)

questions.q: **P** is the mother of **Q**. Q is married to **R**. R is the father of **S** and **T**. **U** is the brother of R. How is U related to Q?
questions.solution: R is the father of S and T and is married to Q, so Q is R's wife. U is R's brother, i.e. U is the brother of Q's husband — Q's **brother-in-law**. (U is the uncle of S and T, not of Q; P and S, T are extra information.)
questions.shortcut: Husband's brother = brother-in-law; ignore the extra names.

questions.q:
**A + B** means A is the father of B; **A − B** means A is the wife of B; **A × B** means A is the brother of B; **A ÷ B** means A is the daughter of B.

Which of the following expressions means that **R is the maternal uncle of T**?
questions.solution:
Maternal uncle = brother of T's **mother**. Check each option:

- **R × P − Q + T:** R is the brother of P, P is the wife of Q, Q is the father of T — so P is T's mother and R is her brother ✓
- R × Q + T: R is the brother of T's **father** Q — paternal uncle ✗
- R + P − Q + T: R is the **father** of T's mother P — maternal grandfather ✗
- T ÷ P × R: T is the daughter of P and P is the brother of R, so P is T's father — R is on the father's side ✗
questions.shortcut: Work backwards from T: find T's mother first, then look for her brother.

questions.q: **Rohan** walks 12 m towards west, turns right and walks 5 m, turns right again and walks 20 m, and then turns right once more and walks 11 m. How far and in which direction is he from his starting point?
questions.solution: Start at (0, 0). West 12 m: (−12, 0). Facing west, a right turn faces **north**: 5 m gives (−12, 5). Right again faces **east**: 20 m gives (8, 5). Right again faces **south**: 11 m gives (8, −6). Distance = √(8² + 6²) = **10 m**; he is east and south of the start, so **South-East**.
questions.shortcut: Net east 20 − 12 = 8, net south 11 − 5 = 6; 6-8-10 triplet.

questions.q: In a row of girls, **Rita** is 12th from the left end and **Mona** is 18th from the right end. There are exactly **5 girls between** them. What is the **minimum** possible number of girls in the row?
questions.solution:
Two cases.

- **Mona to the right of Rita:** Mona is 12 + 5 + 1 = 18th from the left and 18th from the right, so total = 18 + 18 − 1 = 35.
- **Mona to the left of Rita:** Mona is 12 − 5 − 1 = 6th from the left and 18th from the right, so total = 6 + 18 − 1 = 23.

The minimum is **23**. (35 is the maximum — the usual trap.)
questions.shortcut: Minimum = overlapping case: (12 + 18) − (5 + 2) = 23.

questions.q: Seven persons **P, Q, R, S, T, U and V** sit in a row facing north. **S** sits third from the left end. Exactly two persons sit between **S** and **V**. **T** sits to the immediate right of V. **Q** sits at one of the extreme ends, and **U** is an immediate neighbour of Q. **R** is not an immediate neighbour of S. Who sits exactly in the **middle** of the row?
questions.solution: Number the seats 1 to 7 from the left (facing north, right = higher number). S = 3. Two persons between S and V puts V at 6 (seat 0 does not exist). T is immediately right of V: T = 7. Q is at an end, and seat 7 is taken, so Q = 1 and U (next to Q) = 2. Seats 4 and 5 remain for P and R; R cannot be next to S (seat 3), so R = 5 and P = 4. Row: Q, U, S, P, R, V, T. The middle seat (4) is **P**.
questions.shortcut: Fix the definite seat (S), then the chained clue V-T, then the ends.

questions.q:
**Statements:** Some cups are plates. All plates are bowls. No bowl is a spoon.

**Conclusions:**
I. Some cups are not spoons.
II. All bowls being cups is a possibility.

Which of the conclusions follow(s)?
questions.solution: The cups that are plates are also bowls, and no bowl is a spoon — so those cups are definitely not spoons: I **follows**. For II, nothing stops the Cups circle from covering the whole Bowls circle (cups and spoons have no restriction that clashes), so the possibility holds: II **follows**. Answer: **Both**.
questions.shortcut: Definite chain Some → All → No gives 'Some ... not'; a possibility follows whenever no statement forbids it.

questions.solution: Some teenagers are students and some are not, so Teenagers and Students **overlap**. Some senior citizens are also students (adult learners), so Students and Senior citizens **overlap**. But no one can be a teenager and a senior citizen at the same time, so those two circles are **separate**. The diagram with three circles in a chain — middle one overlapping both, outer two apart — fits.
questions.shortcut: Decide each pair separately: overlap, inside, or apart; then match the picture.

questions.q:
When the following words are arranged as in an English dictionary, which word comes **third**?

**Harbour, Harmony, Hardware, Harvest, Harness**
questions.solution: All words start with **Har**; compare the 4th letter: Har**b**our (b), Har**d**ware (d), Har**m**ony (m), Har**n**ess (n), Har**v**est (v). Order: Harbour, Hardware, **Harmony**, Harness, Harvest. Third = **Harmony**.
questions.shortcut: Common prefix — rank by the first letter that differs.

questions.q:
**Statement:** A notice near the lifts of an office building reads: "In case of fire, use the staircase. Do not use the lifts."

**Assumptions:**
I. Lifts may be unsafe to use during a fire.
II. Without the notice, some people might try to use the lifts during a fire.

Which of the assumptions is/are implicit in the statement?
options: Neither I nor II is implicit
Both I and II are implicit
questions.solution: The instruction to avoid lifts only makes sense if lifts may be unsafe in a fire — I is implicit. A notice is put up only when the writer expects that people might otherwise do the wrong thing — II is implicit too. Answer: **Both**.
questions.shortcut: Ask: 'Why would anyone write this?' — every reason the writer takes for granted is an implicit assumption.

questions.q: How many triangles are there in the given figure?
questions.figure: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 154 118" width="154" height="118" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.5" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round"><line x1="77" y1="5" x2="5" y2="113"/><line x1="5" y1="113" x2="149" y2="113"/><line x1="149" y1="113" x2="77" y2="5"/><line x1="77" y1="5" x2="53" y2="113"/><line x1="77" y1="5" x2="101" y2="113"/><line x1="53" y1="41" x2="101" y2="41"/><line x1="29" y1="77" x2="125" y2="77"/></svg>
questions.solution:
Two lines run from the top vertex to the base, and two lines cut across parallel to the base.

Lines through the top vertex = 2 sides + 2 inner lines = 4. Any two of them, together with one horizontal line below the vertex, make a triangle: C(4, 2) = 6 triangles for **each** horizontal line. There are 3 horizontal lines (the base and the two cross lines), so the total is 6 × 3 = **18**. (Counting only the base layer gives 6, and base + one cross line gives 12.)
questions.shortcut: For k apex lines and h cross lines: (k + 1)(k + 2)/2 × (h + 1) = 6 × 3 = 18.

questions.solution: In a water image the order of the characters stays the same and each character is flipped **upside down**. K, B and E are top-bottom symmetric, so they look unchanged; R, 4 and 7 appear inverted. The option that keeps the order and inverts every character is correct.
questions.shortcut: Water image: same order, each character turned upside down (not left-right).

questions.solution: The sheet is folded along one diagonal (into a triangle) and then along the other diagonal (into a quarter-triangle); the punch goes through all four layers near the middle of the bottom edge. Unfolding the second fold reflects the hole across the second diagonal, giving a hole near the middle of the left edge. Unfolding the first fold reflects both across the first diagonal, giving holes near the middle of the right and top edges. Result: **4 holes**, one near the middle of each edge.
questions.shortcut: Two diagonal folds = 4 layers; the final pattern is symmetric about both diagonals.

questions.q: Three different positions of the same dice are shown. Which number is on the face opposite to **1**? (Ignore the orientation of the letters/numbers.)
questions.figure: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 189 59" width="189" height="59" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.3" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round"><polygon points="4,21 38,21 38,55 4,55"/><polygon points="4,21 38,21 55,4 21,4"/><polygon points="38,21 55,4 55,38 38,55"/><text x="21" y="43" font-size="14" text-anchor="middle" fill="currentColor" stroke="none" font-family="sans-serif">2</text><text x="29.5" y="16.5" font-size="10" text-anchor="middle" fill="currentColor" stroke="none" font-family="sans-serif">1</text><text x="46.5" y="33.5" font-size="10" text-anchor="middle" fill="currentColor" stroke="none" font-family="sans-serif">3</text><polygon points="69,21 103,21 103,55 69,55"/><polygon points="69,21 103,21 120,4 86,4"/><polygon points="103,21 120,4 120,38 103,55"/><text x="86" y="43" font-size="14" text-anchor="middle" fill="currentColor" stroke="none" font-family="sans-serif">5</text><text x="94.5" y="16.5" font-size="10" text-anchor="middle" fill="currentColor" stroke="none" font-family="sans-serif">1</text><text x="111.5" y="33.5" font-size="10" text-anchor="middle" fill="currentColor" stroke="none" font-family="sans-serif">2</text><polygon points="134,21 168,21 168,55 134,55"/><polygon points="134,21 168,21 185,4 151,4"/><polygon points="168,21 185,4 185,38 168,55"/><text x="151" y="43" font-size="14" text-anchor="middle" fill="currentColor" stroke="none" font-family="sans-serif">1</text><text x="159.5" y="16.5" font-size="10" text-anchor="middle" fill="currentColor" stroke="none" font-family="sans-serif">6</text><text x="176.5" y="33.5" font-size="10" text-anchor="middle" fill="currentColor" stroke="none" font-family="sans-serif">3</text></svg>
questions.solution: Collect every number seen **next to 1**: view 1 shows 2 and 3, view 2 shows 5 and 2, view 3 shows 6 and 3. So 2, 3, 5 and 6 are all adjacent to 1. A face has exactly four neighbours, so the only number left, **4**, is opposite 1.
questions.shortcut: List the neighbours of the asked face; the missing number is opposite.
